fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Access Drive; Front Entry Area; Open Lawn Area; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Long Driveway
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point during low-visibility or nighttime conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Maintain a minimum vertical clearance along the entire driveway to allow fire apparatus and other large vehicles to pass through without stopping.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responding units can reach the residence without delay.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the residence so apparatus can exit without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Thin vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around all sides of each building.
• Cut back dense vegetation that narrows or blocks movement between the detached structure and the main residence.
• Clear a walkable path along the rear of the residence so responders can reach the back of the structure without pushing through overgrown areas.
• Keep any gate or barrier on the access drive unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lock box so responders can enter without delay.
• Trim vegetation near the front entry area so responders can clearly see and reach the main door on arrival.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Tall Grass Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation; Ground Vegetation; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the building.
• Cut tall grass areas close to the structure down to a short, mowed height.
• Remove accumulated dead grass and dry plant material from the ground around the structure.
• Clear brush growing within close range of the structure to increase separation between the brush and the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Mow or cut grass along the edges of the driveway to keep it from narrowing the travel path.
• Separate groups of shrubs near the structure so they are not touching or overlapping each other.
• Remove dead or dry material from within mixed vegetation areas that are closest to the structure.
• Keep ground vegetation immediately surrounding the structure short and sparse throughout the fire season.
